prompt:
Produce up to 4 distinct, useful design or engineering actions for the task below. Explore materially different mechanisms, including non-obvious alternatives. Respect every constraint. Give executable changes in the target domain, with an implementation step and a falsifiable check. Do not claim unmeasured gains, invent supporting facts, or rename the same action several ways. State actions in the user's terms; omit donor names and analogy explanations from the answer. Fewer actions, including none, are acceptable when no additional valid action remains. Keep each action compact: aim for 60–80 words TOTAL across its five fields, never more than 110. Suggested field budgets: action 8 words, mechanism 16, implementation 22, check 20, risk 10. The 110-word maximum applies to the SUM of all five values, not to each field.

Task:
{
  "title": "Shared kiosk interruption",
  "brief": "Design a museum ticket kiosk flow for visitors who may need several minutes to read each screen. A session currently clears after 90 seconds, losing selected tickets. The next visitor must not see the previous visitor's selections. Staff can help but cannot monitor every kiosk.",
  "constraints": [
    "No accounts, camera, phone, or biometric identification.",
    "Kiosk has a touch screen, physical Back/Confirm buttons, and a screen reader.",
    "A purchase is not submitted until the visitor explicitly confirms; abandoned personal details must not be shown to a new visitor.",
    "Must work without a network for up to ten minutes."
  ],
  "success_criteria": [
    "A slow visitor can complete without repeatedly reconstructing selections.",
    "A new visitor can start safely after abandonment.",
    "Describe an observable way to test the tradeoff between interruption and privacy."
  ],
  "non_goals": [
    "Changing ticket prices or adding staffed kiosks."
  ]
}
Optional outside cue:
Donor domain: Archival provenance and original order
Relation: Records gain meaning from who created them and how they were grouped in the originating activity. Preserving those relationships supports interpretation even when a new arrangement would look tidier. Description can expose access paths without silently replacing the evidence of the original organization.
Boundary: An original order may be unknown, disrupted, or unsuitable for direct browsing. Do not invent one or treat historical organization as infallible; distinguish preserved evidence from a newly constructed access view.
Treat the relation as an optional prompt for exploration. Transfer useful relationships, not surface nouns. The donor is not evidence that a target intervention will work. Ignore the cue if it cannot support a valid move.

Return JSON only: {"actions":[{"action":"...","mechanism":"...","implementation":"...","check":"...","risk":"..."}],"abstention_reason":""}. Use abstention_reason only to explain an empty action list. No tools or additional research.
